doc.title: Paquito D'Rivera — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Live at Keystone Corner, the second CBS album
summary: Helen Keane arranged a live recording at Todd Barkan's San Francisco club, with Roditi on valve trombone.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: That first record increased your opportunities, that relationship with CBS increased your opportunities. What was your next record after that first one?

The next record was called, Life at Keystone Corner. There was a club owned by Todd Barkan, in San Francisco, wonderful club. People like Archie Shepp played there and Woody Shaw among other great artist. Helen Keane got me that gig, and she was the person to record live there. That was the first time that Claudio Roditi record with me and play the valve trombone, which my favorite brass instrument. A year later he sold the trombone; I say, “Why you do that to me?” He didn’t want to play the trombone anymore.
